title: youtube.json
description: The CHANNEL CATALOG (pipeline/state/youtube.json): every upload on the YouTube channel, keyed by its YouTube video id — what YouTube says it is (title, type, playlists), which content folder it came from, its latest metrics, and the daily reach rows (impressions + CTR) the Reporting API delivers. Written by pipeline/06-publish/fetch-analytics.mjs (1A, D-073). The lifecycle ledger (videos.json) stays the owner of each video's lifecycle; it only receives the youtube_video_id binding and the scheduled snapshots from here.

schema_version.description: Catalog format version. Bump only with a migration.

updated.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) the catalog was last written.

fetched.description: ISO date of the last LIVE fetch from YouTube (null until the first one).

playlist_test.description: 3E — the playlist test: all playlists stay; after 8-10 weeks (and >=3 videos per playlist) the data picks the channel's main promise.

started.description: ISO date the test window opened (stamped on the first fetch).

playlists.description: The channel's own playlists as YouTube lists them, keyed by playlist id.

reach.description: The YouTube Reporting API job that delivers thumbnail impressions + CTR (report type channel_reach_basic_a1). Its daily CSV reports expire after 30-60 days, so every row is kept in videos[].reach_daily.

job_id.description: Reporting job id; null until the job exists.

job_created.description: ISO date the job was created (first reports ~48h later, plus a 30-day backfill).

ingested.description: Report ids already merged — so a re-run never double-counts a day.

status.description: Last outcome in plain words (e.g. 'ok', 'api disabled', 'waiting for the first report').

videos.description: One record per upload, keyed by the YouTube video id.

title.description: The title as it is live on YouTube (the owner may rename at upload).

published_at.description: ISO date YouTube reports for the upload.

scheduled_for.description: ISO date a scheduled (still private) upload goes public — YouTube status.publishAt. The publish schedule (3D, D-074) counts the slot on this day, not on the upload day.

content_type.description: From the Analytics API creatorContentType (shorts / videoOnDemand); null while YouTube has no views to classify it by and its length can't tell.

content_key.description: The content folder this upload came from — the ledger key shape ("024-frozen", "024-frozen/short", legacy "002-short"). null = not mapped yet (fetch-analytics --map <ytId> <key>).

key_source.description: How content_key was set: auto-matched on the title, by hand (--map), or deliberately left without a folder (--map <id> none — e.g. a folder's second Short). manual and none are never re-matched.

metrics.description: Lifetime metrics as of `fetched` (YouTube Analytics API; impressions + CTR from the reach rows).

retention_pct.description: averageViewPercentage (0..100; a looping Short can exceed 100).

impressions.description: Sum of the daily thumbnail impressions kept in reach_daily.

ctr.description: Impression-weighted click-through rate, as a FRACTION (0.05 = 5%).

traffic.description: Views by traffic source (insightTrafficSourceType → views), e.g. SHORTS, YT_SEARCH, RELATED_VIDEO.

reach_daily.description: Daily reach rows, date (YYYY-MM-DD) → [impressions, ctr exactly as the report delivered it]. Kept because the reports themselves expire.
